raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Keep Qwen3-VL image encoder CUDA graphs available when video pruning is configured. Append the image mRoPE metadata outside the captured vision forward, using the same helper as eager encoding and retaining the complete DeepStack output.

Related: #38175. This is separate from #63951 (skipping capture when no modalities are eligible), #60112 (replay-capacity fallback), and #49432 (encoder interface refactoring). Open PR searches for encoder/cudagraph/pruning and image pruning found no equivalent image postprocessing change.

## Claims

- With EVS or VidCom2 configured, image encoding can use encoder CUDA graphs in the default `mm_encoder_tp_mode="weights"` mode when the configured image limit is positive.
- The five image position channels are appended after replay or eager fallback, with all visual and DeepStack channels preserved.
- Returned embeddings own their storage and survive later replays. Video encoding and pruning with encoder data parallelism remain eager.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Baseline production source with the image regression | Failed: images were not an eligible graph modality |
| Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3.5-0.8B, EVS and VidCom2, `TRITON_ATTN` | 4 passed in 421.84 s with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` |
| Additional Qwen3-VL EVS `FLASH_ATTN` variant, including disabled-image configuration | 1 passed in 62.66 s with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` |
| Disabled-image configuration before its guard | Failed: advertised `["image"]` instead of `[]` |
| Pre-commit, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering | Passed |

One NVIDIA RTX 4090 24 GB; Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers 5.20.2, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1. Python source base: `5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9`. Native libraries and packaged submodule files came from the official `6fe3d447ac6429ef13aff117744d0298e28879ed` cu130 wheel; the intervening commit only changes Mistral chat templating. Both comparison arms use the same native files.

Real checkpoints:

- `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, revision `89644892e4d85e24eaac8bacfd4f463576704203`.
- `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, revision `2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17`.

```bash
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py \
  -k test_pruned_image_encoder_cudagraph -v -s
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py \
  docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md
```

The new regression checks real graph hits for one and two distinct images, an oversized-image eager fallback, exact position metadata, preservation of all visual channels, retained outputs across subsequent replays, and 16-token greedy generation with top-5 logprob comparisons against encoder-CG-disabled execution. It uses MRV2 and `TRITON_ATTN`; the existing Buildkite core-model selection covers this file. The additional local variant changes the backend to `FLASH_ATTN` and temporarily sets the real model's public image-limit configuration to `ImageDummyOptions(count=0)`, checking that `get_encoder_cudagraph_config().modalities` becomes empty, then restores the original configuration.

## Details

Pruning currently disables both graph modalities because image and video eager postprocessing add position metadata that the raw graph output lacks. Image postprocessing has a fixed five-channel format, so it can run after the existing graph and fallback paths. This change enables images in weights mode and reserves the extra five channels in the advertised output width; video pruning stays outside this scope.

The postprocessor uses CPU grid metadata already selected by the manager, reuses `_postprocess_image_embeds_evs`, and scatters outputs back to their original item indices. Concatenating the position channels creates owned output tensors, so an additional clone is unnecessary. An image limit of zero leaves both graph modalities disabled, composing with #63951 for video-only deployments.

Tensor comparisons use matching execution shapes. An initial test accidentally compared two separate 64-token forwards with a single batched 128-token forward. A control reproduced the same differences in eager alone, while each graph output was bit-exact with its corresponding separate eager forward. The regression now captures 64 and 128 token budgets; no numerical tolerance was widened.

Coverage gaps: full video-pruning generation, multi-GPU execution, MoE checkpoints, MRV1, and other GPU architectures. No latency or memory-saving percentage is claimed. An exploratory FlashInfer run hit its existing `return_lse=True` assertion before exercising the new postprocessor.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, tests and validation. The reported remote runs were executed by an AI agent on the submitter's server.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -139,7 +139,7 @@ When `mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"`, the manager distributes images across TP ranks
 Following <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35963> (ViT full CUDA graph support for image inference), <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38061> extends the encoder CUDA graph framework to support video inference for Qwen3-VL. Previously, the CUDA graph capture/replay path only handled image inputs (`pixel_values` + `image_grid_thw`). Video inputs use different keys (`pixel_values_videos` + `video_grid_thw`) and require larger `cu_seqlens` buffers because each video item contributes multiple frames (`T` attention sequences). This PR generalizes the protocol and manager to handle both modalities through a single shared graph manager.
 
 !!! note
-    Video CUDA graphs are automatically disabled when video token pruning (EVS or VidCom2) is enabled, since pruning makes the token count data-dependent and incompatible with CUDA graph capture.
+    With video token pruning (EVS or VidCom2), Qwen3-VL and models inheriting its encoder implementation, including Qwen3.5 and the MoE variants, keep video encoding eager. Image encoding can use CUDA graphs when `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True`, `mm_encoder_tp_mode="weights"` (the default), and the image limit in `limit_mm_per_prompt` is greater than zero. Image mRoPE metadata is appended outside the captured graph, preserving all DeepStack features. When pruning is enabled with `mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"`, both modalities remain eager.
 
     Mixed inputs (image+video) per prompt are also supported now.

         for result in results:
             assert result["stats"][0]["token_budgets"] == token_budgets
         print(f"E-only {model_id}: {results}")
+
+
+def _check_pruned_image_encoder_outputs(worker, batches):
+    import torch
+
+    runner = worker.model_runner
+    manager = runner.model_state.encoder_runner.cudagraph_manager
+    assert manager is not None and manager.is_captured()
+    assert manager.supports_modality("image")
+    assert not manager.supports_modality("video")
+    hidden_size = runner.model.visual.out_hidden_size
+    assert manager.config.out_hidden_size == hidden_size + 5
+    retained: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = []
+    stats = []
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        for batch in batches:
+            kwargs = {key: value.to(runner.device) for key, value in batch.items()}
+            actual = manager.execute(kwargs)
+            expected = runner.model.embed_multimodal(**kwargs)
+            assert len(actual) == len(expected)
+            for output, reference in zip(actual, expected):
+                assert output.shape == reference.shape
+                assert output.shape[-1] == hidden_size + 5
+                assert torch.isfinite(output).all()
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    output[:, :-5], reference[:, :-5], rtol=0.016, atol=0.016
+                )
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    output[:, -5:], reference[:, -5:], rtol=0, atol=0
+                )
+            for output, snapshot in retained:
+                torch.testing.assert_close(output, snapshot, rtol=0, atol=0)
+            retained.extend((output, output.clone()) for output in actual)
+            stats.append(manager.get_cumulative_stats())
+    assert stats[0]["graph_hits"] > 0
+    assert stats[1]["graph_hits"] > stats[0]["graph_hits"]
+    assert stats[2]["graph_misses"] > stats[1]["graph_misses"]
+    assert stats[3]["graph_hits"] > stats[2]["graph_hits"]
+    return stats
+
+
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model_id", ["qwen3_vl", "qwen3_5"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pruning_method", ["evs", "vidcom2"])
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA graphs")
+def test_pruned_image_encoder_cudagraph(
+    model_id, pruning_method, vllm_runner, image_assets, monkeypatch
+):
+    """Keep pruning metadata, DeepStack features and owned outputs across replay."""
+    from transformers import AutoProcessor
+
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER", "1")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION", "1")
+    config = MODEL_CONFIGS[model_id]
+    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(config.model)
+    first, second = [asset.pil_image for asset in image_assets]
+    images = [first.resize((256, 256)), second.resize((256, 256))]
+    batches = [
+        [images[0]],
+        [images[1], images[0]],
+        [second.resize((512, 512))],
+        [images[1]],
+    ]
+    outputs = []
+    for encoder_cudagraph in (False, True):
+        with vllm_runner(
+            config.model,
+            dtype=config.dtype,
+            max_model_len=config.max_model_len,
+            max_num_seqs=1,
+            enable_prefix_caching=False,
+            mm_encoder_attn_backend="TRITON_ATTN",
+            mm_processor_kwargs={"max_pixels": 512 * 512},
+            video_pruning_rate=0.5,
+            video_pruning_method=pruning_method,
+            limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 2, "video": int(model_id == "qwen3_vl")},
+            compilation_config={
+                "mode": 0,
+                "cudagraph_mode": "NONE",
+                "cudagraph_mm_encoder": encoder_cudagraph,
+                "encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets": [64, 128],
+                "encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch": 2,
+                "encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch": 1,
+            },
+        ) as model:
+            if encoder_cudagraph:
+                mm_config = (
+                    model.llm.llm_engine.vllm_config.model_config.multimodal_config
+                )
+                inputs = [
+                    dict(
+                        processor.image_processor(
+                            images=batch,
+                            return_tensors="pt",
+                            **mm_config.merge_mm_processor_kwargs({}),
+                        )
+                    )
+                    for batch in batches
+                ]
+                assert inputs[0]["image_grid_thw"].tolist() == [[1, 16, 16]]
+                assert inputs[1]["image_grid_thw"].tolist() == [[1, 16, 16]] * 2
+                model.llm.collective_rpc(
+                    partial(_check_pruned_image_encoder_outputs, batches=inputs)
+                )
+            outputs.append(
+                model.generate_greedy_logprobs(
+                    [config.image_prompt],
+                    max_tokens=16,
+                    num_logprobs=5,
+                    images=[[images[0]]],
+                )
+            )
+            assert outputs[-1][0][0]
+    check_logprobs_close(
+        outputs_0_lst=outputs[0],
+        outputs_1_lst=outputs[1],
+        name_0="eager",
+        name_1="encoder_cudagraph",
+        always_check_logprobs=True,
+    )

+        if self.is_multimodal_pruning_enabled:
+            image_limit = (
+                self.model_config.get_multimodal_config().get_limit_per_prompt("image")
+            )
+            modalities = (
+                ["image"] if not self.use_data_parallel and image_limit > 0 else []
+            )
 
         # Compute max_frames_per_video for budget sizing.
         max_frames = self.get_max_frames_per_video() if "video" in modalities else 1

             ],
-            out_hidden_size=self.visual.out_hidden_size,
+            out_hidden_size=self.visual.out_hidden_size
+            + (5 if self.is_multimodal_pruning_enabled else 0),

         )
 
@@ -2398,6 +2401,35 @@ def encoder_eager_forward(
         grid_thw = self._get_grid_thw_by_modality(mm_kwargs)
         return self.visual(pixel_values, grid_thw)
 
+    def postprocess_encoder_output(
+        self,
+        outputs: dict[str, torch.Tensor],
+        indices: list[int],
+        per_item_out_tokens: list[int],
+        dest: dict[int, torch.Tensor] | list[torch.Tensor | None],
+        clone: bool = False,
+        batch_mm_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        if not self.is_multimodal_pruning_enabled:
+            return super().postprocess_encoder_output(
+                outputs, indices, per_item_out_tokens, dest, clone, batch_mm_kwargs
+            )
+
+        assert batch_mm_kwargs is not None
+        assert self.get_input_modality(batch_mm_kwargs) == "image"
+        sizes = [per_item_out_tokens[i] for i in indices]
+        image_embeds = outputs["default"][: sum(sizes)].split(sizes)
+        image_input = Qwen2_5_VLImagePixelInputs(
+            type="pixel_values",
+            pixel_values=batch_mm_kwargs["pixel_values"],
+            image_grid_thw=torch.tensor(
+                self._get_grid_thw_by_modality(batch_mm_kwargs), device="cpu"
+            ),
+        )
+        image_embeds = self._postprocess_image_embeds_evs(image_embeds, image_input)
+        for index, embedding in zip(indices, image_embeds):
+            dest[index] = embedding
+
     def _parse_and_validate_image_input(
         self, **kwargs: object
     ) -> Qwen2_5_VLImageInputs | None:
